Gyges Labs recently completed its Pre-A+ funding round, with investments from Granite Asia and Radiant Capital. Following the international success of their jointly launched AI glasses, Halliday, the new funds will primarily support the expansion of a more diverse range of "superhuman gear" (AI wearable products), with related new products set to debut gradually starting in early 2026.

Unlike approaches that aim to replace humans with AI, Gyges Labs is an AI wearable technology company dedicated to "enabling everyone to become a superhuman." The company operates globally, with its headquarters in Singapore, software and AI teams based in Silicon Valley, USA, and leverages China's supply chain advantages, possessing unique technologies such as advanced optics and active AI.

Just as Iron Man and Batman's gear endows ordinary people with superpowers, Gyges Labs believes that applying AI to wearable products, allowing humans to harness AI, makes humans more irreplaceable than directly providing AI with physical capabilities.

Luo Tingxia, founding partner of Radiant Capital, stated: As a next-generation investment firm focused on technology and consumer sectors, we are committed to discovering and supporting companies that define the future. Gyges Labs perfectly embodies this vision. While the smart glasses industry is still exploring forms, they have already positioned themselves at the forefront of the next generation of human-computer interaction with their forward-looking insights into "invisibility" and "proactivity" as core experiences. Their team demonstrates exceptional product definition capabilities and pragmatism.

Convertir a las personas en superhumanos podría ser el enfoque correcto para el paradigma de interacción humano-máquina. A diferencia de quienes buscan que la IA reemplace a la humanidad, Gyges Labs es una empresa tecnológica de dispositivos vestibles de IA comprometida con "permitir que cada persona se convierta en un superhumano". excerpt_i18n.en:
On November 18, Leiphone reported the launch of Zebra Spoken English, the world's first one-on-one AI tutor product for children aged 6 to 12. It features a superhuman AI tutor that provides personalized, full-English instruction, giving each child a dedicated AI tutor. This release marks the transition of large AI models from general exploration to practical application in specific industries, representing the first truly industrialized AI Agent in education. 

The superhuman AI tutor addresses common challenges in children's oral English learning, such as difficulty finding and scheduling human tutors, inconsistent professional standards, and children's reluctance to speak. AI Agents offer advantages like exceptional memory and storage, enabling them to recall every moment of a child's lessons, from speaking performance and knowledge accumulation to unique habits, interests, and personality traits. 

Zebra Spoken English achieves the breakthrough of a leading AI tutor by focusing intensely on the narrow scenario of one-on-one children's oral practice. This requires the AI to possess multiple capabilities: first, speech recognition that understands children, deciphering non-standard accents, fragmented sentences, and jumping thoughts; second, teaching logic that effectively educates children, supported by complex algorithms integrating second language acquisition theory, child cognitive psychology, and extensive teaching cases.
excerpt_i18n.es: Según Leifeng, el 18 de noviembre se lanzó oficialmente "Zebra Oral", el primer producto mundial de tutoría individual de IA para niños de 6 a 12 años. Destacado por su "tutor de IA sobrehumano", ofrece clases individuales totalmente en inglés, permitiendo que cada niño tenga un tutor de IA personalizado. Su lanzamiento marca la transición de los modelos de IA de exploración general a aplicaciones específicas en sectores verticales, siendo el primer agente de IA verdaderamente industrializado en educación. Con el nacimiento del "tutor sobrehumano", surge la pregunta: ¿funcionará el tutor de IA? En el aprendizaje oral infantil, los padres suelen enfrentar dificultades para encontrar y reservar tutores humanos, junto con la inconsistencia en su nivel profesional.

excerpt_i18n.en:
Baidu's Wenku and Netdisk have officially expanded overseas. At this year's Baidu World Conference, in addition to emphasizing "internalized AI," Baidu announced the latest progress in the global rollout of several flagship products. Baidu Wenku and Netdisk are at the forefront, serving as the "vanguard" in Baidu's exploration of the global AI market.

Although large-scale foundational models are developing rapidly and impressively worldwide, creating an "illusion" that AI is all-powerful, the reality is different. Businesses, employees, and students abroad are similarly constrained by the unhealthy "inverted pyramid" structure in the AI industry—more specific and personalized usage scenarios and needs remain largely unmet.

In China, Baidu Wenku, as a one-stop AI content acquisition and creation platform covering work, study, and even entertainment and daily life, has surpassed 90 million monthly active users, firmly leading its sector. However, overseas, products with comprehensive multimodal capabilities are rare—those that integrate understanding, generation, and editing of text, images, audio, and video across the entire process, along with capabilities like task decomposition, path planning, and workflow orchestration. In short, overseas AI products are often vertical and fragmented, making all-in-one solutions like Baidu Wenku nearly impossible to find.

Particularly in regions such as the Middle East, Southeast Asia, and South America, the adoption of AI capabilities remains at levels seen years ago, leaving a significant market gap.

Baidu Netdisk faces similar opportunities. Many overseas Chinese look to it to stay connected with family and friends back home, share life experiences, use AI to preserve shared memories, and build an "online home" that transcends physical distance.

From November 15 to 17, 2025, the main forum of the AI+ Conference, themed "AI's Next Decade: Scenario-Driven × New Quality Engine," was held at the Beijing Zhongguancun International Innovation Center. The event was co-organized by the National High-Tech Zone AI Industry Collaborative Innovation Network, the CCTV "Win in AI+" program team, Tsinghua University's Institute for Sustainable Social Value, Renmin University of China's Institute for Interdisciplinary Sciences, CCID Think Tank's AI Research Center, and Zhongguancun Development Group, with exclusive strategic support from the Zhongguancun Science and Technology Entrepreneurs Association. (Leifeng Network)

Top AI minds converged to discuss AI's next decade. Turing Award winner, academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and dean of Tsinghua University's Institute for Interdisciplinary Information Science and AI School, Yao Qizhi, delivered a keynote speech titled "Future Prospects of Artificial Intelligence." He stated that large AI models are revolutionizing various industries, with the medium to long-term goal being the advancement toward AGI to empower science, while ensuring AI is safe, controllable, and reliable. Its prospects are vast and its impact profound, necessitating continuous innovation and breakthroughs. China has no shortage of application talent and scenarios; the most crucial task is to cultivate more cutting-edge innovative talent.

As a representative of the young vanguard, Wang Xingxing, founder and CEO of Unitree Robotics, shared his deeply held dreams and aspirations in a speech titled "Our Next Decade." He emphasized that the next decade will be one of "growth and blossoming"—where robots evolve from "capable of tasks" to "skilled at tasks," transitioning from "industry tools" to "life partners."

excerpt_i18n.en:
In recent years, the AI industry has moved at an almost surreal pace. Models have repeatedly pushed boundaries, product iterations race against time, and discussions have shifted from "reasoning costs" to "emergent intelligence" and "AGI timelines," with sentiments swinging between optimism and anxiety. Amid such intense technological cycles, few pause to consider a more fundamental question: What kind of intelligence are we truly pursuing? Beyond language, are there abilities not yet fully understood?

A week ago, Li Fei-Fei reignited this debate with a lengthy article on world models, which avoided hype or easy predictions. Its weight lay in highlighting the tough challenges current technology often sidesteps: spatial understanding, physical reasoning, embodied behavior, and real-world uncertainties—long-avoided issues laid out one by one, sparking intense discussions within the AI community on world models.

A week later, in a recent interview, Li Fei-Fei revisited the unresolved points from that article, breaking down questions she had pondered deeply but couldn't fully expand on in writing. She provided more detailed explanations on the structural shortcomings of language models in world understanding, the foundational role of 3D space in intelligence formation, and the unavoidable real-world constraints behind the long stagnation in robotics.

As these fragmented clues were pieced together, the interview served as a continuation and completion of the original article, offering a clearer view of the technical directions she genuinely focuses on and the logic behind them.
excerpt_i18n.es: En los últimos años, el ritmo de la industria de la IA ha sido casi irreal. Los modelos han superado límites repetidamente, la iteración de productos parece una carrera contra el tiempo, y los debates han oscilado entre el "coste del razonamiento", la "emergencia de la inteligencia" y los "plazos para la AGI", con emociones balanceándose entre el optimismo y la ansiedad. En ciclos tecnológicos tan intensos, pocos se detienen a reflexionar sobre una cuestión más fundamental: ¿qué tipo de inteligencia estamos buscando realmente? Más allá del lenguaje, ¿existen capacidades aún no comprendidas a fondo? Hace una semana, Fei-Fei Li rescató este tema con un extenso artículo sobre modelos del mundo, que no exageró la revolución ni ofreció un futuro sencillo; su peso radica en señalar que la tecnología actual está eludiendo algo.

excerpt_i18n.en: In the second half of 2025, two notable trends emerged in discussions within the U.S.-China AI community. First, the focus shifted from debating the generational gap in technology between the two nations to acknowledging the rise of China's AI capabilities, with some anticipating an imminent overtaking. For instance, overseas companies like Airbnb publicly stated they heavily adopted Tongyi Qianwen over OpenAI, while MiniMax's open-source model M2 surpassed Claude in AI coding capabilities, ranking among the top three in programming on OpenRouter. Second, capital speculation and bubble risks intensified significantly—OpenAI and Nvidia signed a $1.4 trillion computing power order, and a remark by OpenAI's CFO about needing government guarantees for AI investments triggered a major sell-off in U.S. tech stocks, wiping out nearly $800 billion in market value from eight major tech giants in a week. The former trend points to the market, indicating that demand is no longer blindly pursuing peak intelligence but opting for cost-effective, faster Chinese models; the latter highlights capital, revealing that the U.S. AI industry faces serious scrutiny over high valuations and massive capital expenditures, with investors growing uneasy and panicked about the high-stakes, high-investment model requiring continuous funding for startups. Both phenomena signify that the AI narrative once dominated by U.S. tech giants like OpenAI is beginning to shift.
excerpt_i18n.es: En la segunda mitad de 2025, se observaron dos fenómenos interesantes en los círculos de IA de China y EE. UU.: primero, el enfoque dejó de ser cuántas generaciones separan la tecnología de ambos países para reconocer el auge de la IA china e incluso su inminente superación, como empresas extranjeras representadas por Airbnb que admiten usar masivamente Tongyi Qianwen en lugar de OpenAI, y el modelo abierto M2 de MiniMax, cuya capacidad de codificación supera a Claude y se sitúa entre las tres primeras en habilidad de programación de OpenRouter. Segundo, las apuestas arriesgadas de capital y los riesgos de burbuja se intensificaron notablemente.
